questions.q: In Apex, what type does a SOSL search with a multi-object RETURNING clause return?
options: AggregateResult
A single List<SObject>
List<List<SObject>>
Map<String, List<SObject>>
questions.explain: A SOSL search returns an outer list with one inner list per object type listed in RETURNING, in the order they were listed.

questions.q: In FIND 'Acme' RETURNING Account(Id, Name), Contact(Id, FirstName), what does searchResults[1] correspond to?
options: An error — SOSL results are not indexable
The Account results
A combined list of both objects
The Contact results
questions.explain: Position in the returned List<List<SObject>> matches the order objects were listed in RETURNING — Account is index 0, Contact is index 1.

questions.q: Can each object inside a multi-object RETURNING clause have its own WHERE and LIMIT?
options: Yes — each object's sub-clause can be filtered and capped independently of the others
No — WHERE and LIMIT can only apply to the whole search, not per object
Only LIMIT can be set per object, never WHERE
Only the first object listed can have a WHERE or LIMIT
questions.explain: Each object named in RETURNING can carry its own independent WHERE and LIMIT, letting you tune each object's slice of the search separately.

questions.q: What restriction applies to using OFFSET in a SOSL search?
options: It can be used freely in any multi-object RETURNING search
It can only be used when the search targets a single object, and must be the last clause in that object's sub-clause
OFFSET is not supported in SOSL at all
OFFSET in SOSL has no row cap, unlike SOQL
questions.explain: SOSL's OFFSET only works for a single-object search and must be the final clause for that object — it cannot be combined with a multi-object RETURNING search.

questions.q: What is a real risk when editing a multi-object SOSL search's RETURNING clause later in a codebase?
options: Apex will throw a compile-time error if the RETURNING order changes
SOSL automatically re-sorts RETURNING objects alphabetically, so order never matters
Changing the object order or count without updating the Apex indexing can silently misalign which list corresponds to which object
There is no risk, since SOSL results are always returned as a labeled map
questions.explain: Because the Apex result is positional (List<List<SObject>>), editing RETURNING's object order or count without updating corresponding Apex indices is a real, common source of bugs.
